question: Which controls make an internal data release decision reviewable and reversible?

documents.title: Immutable Dataset Identity
documents.full_text: A release record binds the dataset to an immutable snapshot digest. Reviewers can reconstruct the exact bytes instead of relying on a moving folder.

documents.title: Named Approval
documents.full_text: A named owner records approval only after inspecting the retained evidence. The decision log includes the reviewer, time, and explicit limitations.

documents.title: Reversible Publication
documents.full_text: A staged release keeps the prior dataset available and documents a tested rollback procedure. Publication stops when rollback cannot be demonstrated.

documents.title: Adverse Data Control
documents.full_text: A deliberately malformed record must be rejected even when the import command reports success. The adverse control proves validation observes the artifact rather than an exit code.

documents.title: Raw Audit Trail
documents.full_text: Raw validation output, warnings, and failed checks remain attached to the release decision. A summary never replaces the underlying audit trail.

documents.title: Compost for Raised Beds
documents.full_text: Finished compost improves soil structure in raised vegetable beds. Gardeners mix it into the upper layer before spring planting.

documents.title: Cooling Sourdough Bread
documents.full_text: Fresh sourdough should cool on a rack before slicing. The crumb continues setting as steam leaves the loaf.
